note: claude-opus-5-5、入力 3516 / 出力 2116 トークン

data.question: Should block_k be lowered from 3 to 2 by overriding the 1-2 company vote (A for; B and C against), given that it is resubmitted under rush load without the remedy for C or the road-violation breakdown you asked for in D1, or should v1 stay in place?
data.background: In D1 you declined to override a 1-2 vote on this same change. You asked for it to return with a remedy for C and a breakdown of the added road violations. The change passes check, the constitution and the KPI gates again, with a larger rush-period gain, but it lost the vote again and still comes with no remedy for C and no per-company breakdown of road violations or sanctions. Whether a bigger customer gain justifies overriding a two-of-three majority, and accepting extra violations and Major eviction sanctions that fall mostly on C, is a governance judgment that only you can make.

options.summary: Adopt block_k 3 → 2 over the vote. On-time goes from 216.6 to 223.8 (+7.2, 5/5 seeds improved) and late from 11.4 to 4.2. Blocked s falls from 1824 to 936, p95_wait_s from 138 to 110, max_wait_s from 411 to 201, and unfinished stays at 0.0. The lowest on-time rate rises from 0.93 to 0.97. Road violations rise from 19.0 to 28.0, and these have not been broken down by company. Utility moves from 69.8 / 68.5 / 65.8 to 73.4 / 65.5 / 56.3. This would be the first time a 2-of-3 majority vote is overridden.
options.stakeholders: Customers gain: more deliveries are on time, and waits are shorter, especially the worst-case wait (411 → 201 s). Company A gains (+3.6 utility). Company B loses a little (-3.0). Company C loses heavily (-9.5) and is believed to bear most of the eviction sanctions. Governance credibility is put at risk because the companies' vote would be overridden without the remedy you asked for. Road safety and order may suffer from 9 more violations per run, of unknown type.

options.summary: Stay at v1 (block_k 3). The metrics stay at the current row: on-time 216.6, late 11.4, blocked s 1824, road violations 19.0, p95_wait_s 138, max_wait_s 411, unfinished 0.0, utility 69.8 / 68.5 / 65.8. The measured gain is given up for this period, and the D1 request (a remedy for C plus a violation and sanction breakdown) stays open for a future proposal.
options.stakeholders: Companies B and C keep their current utility, and their vote is respected. Company A forgoes +3.6 utility. Customers keep getting the slower service: 7.2 fewer on-time deliveries and 7.2 more late ones per run than option 1, and a worst-case wait of 411 s instead of 201 s. The precedent of not overriding votes is preserved.

recommendation.reason: Option 1 is clearly better for customers and the KPI: on-time 223.8 vs 216.6, late 4.2 vs 11.4, max_wait_s 201 vs 411. However, the conditions you set in D1 are still not met. There is no remedy for C, whose utility falls from 65.8 to 56.3, and no per-company breakdown of the road violations (19.0 → 28.0) or the Major eviction sanctions. Overriding the vote now would set the precedent you wanted to avoid, based on the same missing analysis. The next step should be a block_k=2 variant paired with a remedy for C (for example, softer sanctions for evictions or a compensating rule), measured together with the violation breakdown, so the companies can accept it. If you judge that the larger rush-period gain on its own outweighs the vote, option 1 is the KPI-maximizing alternative.
assumptions: The current row reflects rush-period load that will persist into the next period.
The additional road violations under block_k=2 are mainly eviction-related Major sanctions applied to C's robots, as stated in the reason for referral, but this has not been verified by a breakdown.
A remedy for C can be designed without losing most of the on-time gain.
B's and C's votes reflect their utility losses and would not change without a remedy.

unknowns: The per-company breakdown of road violations and Major sanctions under block_k=2, including how much falls on C.
Whether any remedy for C exists that keeps most of the +7.2 gain and would win B's or C's vote.
Why B votes against despite only a -3.0 utility loss, and how the companies' policies would respond to an override.
How long rush-period demand will last and what demand looks like next period.
How customers perceive the current 411 s worst-case wait and the 11.4 late deliveries per run.
The safety significance of the additional road violations.
